conversation.text:
Description: In a private conversation in the Dining room, Martha Galley and John Hobbes confirm the invitation’s source is abnormal, and introduce the “Chapel key” as a clear new clue and the next action arrangement.
Location: Dining room (Dining room)
Key Information:
  - The conversation takes place in the Dining room (Dining room).
  - Martha Galley explicitly states she has never heard of “Rupert Galley (Rupert Galley)” and denies he is a family member.
  - Martha Galley explains that Galley is not her original surname, and that she adopted it later.
  - Martha Galley speculates that the invitation may have been sent by someone who lived here before she moved into the villa (speculation).
  - Martha Galley confirms there are eleven people in the villa tonight (including the butler Harry Thornton), not counting the stranger who died in the Study.
  - John Hobbes finds a key near the corpse and believes it may not belong to anyone in the house.
  - Martha Galley confirms the key is for the Chapel (Chapel).
  - Martha Galley asks John Hobbes to hand the key to the butler Harry Thornton in the Study.
Characters:
  [Martha Galley (Martha)] Person No. 5, one of the villa residents, responsible for hosting and arranging.
    · Explicitly states she has never heard of anyone named Rupert Galley.
    · Explains that Galley is not her original surname and that she adopted it later.
    · Speculates that if Rupert Galley truly existed, he may have lived here before she moved in and sent the invitation (speculation).
    · Confirms there are eleven people in the villa tonight (including the butler Harry Thornton), not counting the stranger who died in the Study.
    · Identifies the item John Hobbes found as the key to the Chapel (Chapel).
    · Asks John Hobbes to give the key to Harry Thornton.
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, the visitor.
    · Explains he came because of the invitation and wants to understand its source.
    · Finds a key near the corpse and hands it to Martha Galley for identification.
    · Accepts Martha Galley’s arrangement and prepares to hand the key to Harry Thornton.
  [Harry Thornton (Thornton)] The villa’s butler, the only servant in the villa.
    · Is designated as the recipient of the Chapel key.
  [Rupert Galley (Rupert Galley)] The signatory on the invitation.
    · Is explicitly denied by Martha Galley as being related to her family or any current resident.
    · Is believed to possibly be connected to earlier occupants of the villa (speculation).
